_comment: The Tier 1 auto-fix list (spec Section 6.2/6.3). This list is DATA, shipped from the repo, NEVER hand-edited on a box. Qualification bar for tier 1: the signature is unambiguous (a hard evidence predicate, not a heuristic), the fix has succeeded on a real incident at least once, the fix is reversible in one line, and the blast radius is the looping unit only. tier 2 = fix-with-operator-stamp (config-shape change); tier 3 = never-auto (propose and hold).

fix_classes.title: stale-lock removal (dead-pid-proven, JSON-parsed)
fix_classes.proof: the session-health failure defines the safe version (parse with a real parser; dead-pid proof required; never touch a live lock)

fix_classes.title: telegram offset rewind + channel restart
fix_classes.proof: shipped and running fleet-wide since v10.14.5 (telegram-offset-healthcheck.sh)

fix_classes.title: orphan-gateway clear + kickstart (marker archive -> port kill -> kickstart -> stability watch)
fix_classes.proof: the Box E verified 4-step procedure; kill-list contains ONLY the orphan pid

fix_classes.title: cron park on breaker trip (disable, never delete)
fix_classes.proof: the loop-detector / furnace-watch encoded rule (disable never delete)

fix_classes.title: light-context set on a bloating resume cron
fix_classes.proof: the encoded loop-detector fix (740,269 input tokens/tick -> 0)

fix_classes.title: process-unit park on process-breaker trip + boot-log capture
fix_classes.reversible_in: unpark the unit (single start + stability watch)
fix_classes.proof: stop-and-flag is strictly safer than the status quo (infinite respawn)

fix_classes.title: config restore from last-good snapshot on validate-fail (as box user)
fix_classes.reversible_in: the snapshot IS the revert; the prior file is itself snapshotted first

fix_classes.title: heartbeat isolation on a confirmed idle-burn P1: isolatedSession=true + lightContext=true (PREPARED PROPOSAL - never applied by the unattended tick)
fix_classes.reversible_in: restore the PRIOR values of agents.defaults.heartbeat.isolatedSession and agents.defaults.heartbeat.lightContext (read them with the snapshot_before commands first; set them back with --strict-json, or `openclaw config unset <path>` when they were unset)
fix_classes.proof: Source: OpenClaw docs gateway/config-agents/heartbeat-compaction-and-streaming.md lines 22-49. isolatedSession=true runs each heartbeat in a fresh session with no conversation history; the doc says it reduces per-heartbeat token cost from ~100K to ~2-5K tokens. lightContext=true makes heartbeat runs skip the workspace bootstrap files. Separate operator choice, NOT part of this proposal: every: "0m" stops the recurring heartbeat cadence (event-driven wakes can still run one turn). Tier 2 STAYS Tier 2: the watchdog prepares the two commands + the revert and sends them to the OPERATOR for an `approve <finding-id>`; the unattended tick never applies them, and no client box is changed without that stamp. The proposal touches only the two keys listed in touches_only - no provider, no credential, nothing the client chose.

superseded_text.title: heartbeat allowlist flip on a confirmed idle-burn P1
superseded_text.reversible_in: restore the prior heartbeat block (snapshot revert line)
superseded_text.proof: applied twice (operator box, Box C). STARTS as Tier 2 on client boxes; graduates to Tier 1 per box AFTER the operator stamps it once (Open Decision T4).

fix_classes.title: abort the self-blocking run through the native sessions.abort RPC to free the conversation lane (PREPARED PROPOSAL - never applied by the unattended tick)
fix_classes.do_not_set: clearQueued - the user's own follow-up messages are queued behind the blocked run and must keep their place; clearQueued:true would discard them
fix_classes.reversible_in: nothing to revert - aborting a doomed run starts no new state; a call with no active run returns a no-active-run result and changes nothing
fix_classes.proof: NOT AUTO (Tier 2 stays Tier 2: the watchdog PREPARES the operator action and the unattended tick never executes it). Re-pointed for OpenClaw 2026.9.x: sessions.abort and chat.abort now exist as gateway-mediated RPCs (docs web/control-ui/chat.md, Stop button section; docs gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control.md line 41 gives the params: key, optional runId, agentId, clearQueued). The call goes through the running gateway and touches no file. A session-wide sessions.abort also requests cancellation of the session's descendant runs (docs tools/subagents/operations.md). The harm it addresses is unchanged: a blocked run holds the conversation lane for its whole life while the user's messages queue behind it. On OpenClaw 2026.9.x the built-in tool-loop guard (docs tools/loop-detection.md) ends a run after the second critical loop in the same run when the guard is enabled; this class is the after-the-fact abort for a box where that guard is off or the run is stuck anyway.

superseded_text.title: abort the self-blocking run to free the conversation lane
superseded_text.reversible_in: nothing to revert - aborting a doomed run starts no new state
superseded_text.proof: NOT AUTO. As of OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 no supported run-abort CLI was found (`openclaw sessions` offers cleanup/compact/export-trajectory/list only), so this class PREPARES the operator action and never executes one. The harm it addresses is measured: a blocked run holds the conversation lane for its whole life (observed bursts up to 275 blocks) while the user's messages queue behind it, and the runtime - not the model - ended 7 of 10 observed bursts by aborting. The model does not talk its own way out.

fix_classes.title: reset the loop-poisoned session through the running gateway (sessions.reset, history preserved) - PREPARED PROPOSAL; never moves a file
preconditions: the session has NO active run: a reset interrupts work, so it is never applied to a session with an active run (abort it first via LF-9, or do nothing)

expectedSessionId is the session's CURRENT id from sessions.list or sessions.describe, so the gateway refuses the reset with session-changed if the session moved on (docs gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control.md line 44)
fix_classes.graduates_to_tier_1: only after sessions.reset has been proven on the operator box (spec Fix 13 item 3); until then it is a prepared proposal
fix_classes.reversible_in: nothing is deleted: sessions.reset preserves transcript history (docs tools/progress-card.md, reset section); there is no un-reset, the fresh conversation start is the intended effect. For the archive alternative run it with --dry-run first.
fix_classes.proof: OpenClaw 2026.9.x keeps conversations in a per-agent database (docs concepts/session.md), not in files, so there is no transcript file to move and a direct file move is forbidden: both commands go through the RUNNING gateway. Config-FREE and blast-radius-of-one: it touches the one named session, no client config, no model, no credential. Tier 2: KC.apply() never runs an executor for a non-Tier-1 class, so the old file-move executor is not reachable through this class; it only PREPARES the command for an operator `approve <finding-id>`.

superseded_text.title: archive the poisoned session transcript and roll to a fresh one (move, never delete)
superseded_text.reversible_in: move the archived transcript back to its original path
superseded_text.proof: config-FREE and blast-radius-of-one: it moves ONE session transcript aside so the next turn starts clean, touching no client config, no model, and no credential. Guarded by a live-session check (refuses a transcript still being written) so it can never yank a file from under a running gateway. The same move was performed by hand on the operator box during the incident and is the reason a fresh session answered normally.

fix_classes.title: RETIRED - prune compaction checkpoint summaries (OpenClaw 2026.9.x keeps no checkpoint records or files, so there is nothing left to prune)
fix_classes.proof: RETIRED (Skill 61 October update, spec Fix 13 item 4). docs concepts/compaction.md states 'OpenClaw does not create compaction checkpoint records or snapshot copies' (line 227 on 2026.9.8) and that legacy checkpoint files are 'not the active compaction target' (line 167). No supported file-free prune path exists, so this class has no action to prepare. It is kept as a record (disable, never delete) so older findings and ledger rows that name LF-11 still resolve. For a poisoned conversation the supported lever is LF-10.

superseded_text.title: prune compaction checkpoint summaries that captured loop text verbatim
superseded_text.proof: NOT AUTO, deliberately. Poisoned checkpoints are re-injected on resume and SURVIVE a transcript roll (measured: 7 of 16 summaries poisoned), so LF-10 alone does not clear them - but the LIVE gateway rewrites the session store, so an in-place edit without a restart is clobbered. This class prepares the exact prune + its revert for the maintenance path; it is never applied by the unattended tick.

fix_classes.title: abort the resending session via the native sessions.abort RPC with clearQueued:true (no-op-safe when nothing is active) + ledger park flag on the source unit (a visible-red marker only; it stops nothing by itself)
fix_classes.reversible_in: unpark the source unit (clears the ledger flag); sessions.abort has nothing to undo - a call with no active run is a safe no-op. clearQueued:true DISCARDS the source session's queued follow-ups and they cannot be restored; that is intended, so a queued resend cannot restart the work.
fix_classes.proof: the 2026-08-04 incident: sessions_send's hardcoded 30000ms fallback timeout (no timeoutSeconds passed) was misread as delivery failure and resent byte-identical as a brand-new top-level run 6-8x ~34s apart, past 154,000 input tokens with zero brake; config-free (touches no client config, only the one named session), so it applies for real in-tick like LF-6 - never pkill node, never a gateway restart. clearQueued:true is REQUIRED (docs gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control.md line 41 and docs tools/subagents/operations.md): session-wide sessions.abort cancels descendants, but queued follow-ups survive unless clearQueued:true, and without it a queued resend can restart the work. The ledger park flag changes nothing outside Skill 61's own ledger; the abort with clearQueued is what stops the recurrence.

superseded_text.title: abort the resending session via the native sessions.abort RPC (no-op-safe when nothing is active) + park the source unit
superseded_text.reversible_in: unpark the source unit; sessions.abort has nothing to undo - a no-active-run call is already a documented safe no-op (ok=true, abortedRunId=null, status='no-active-run')
superseded_text.proof: the 2026-08-04 incident: sessions_send's hardcoded 30000ms fallback timeout (no timeoutSeconds passed) was misread as delivery failure and resent byte-identical as a brand-new top-level run 6-8x ~34s apart, past 154,000 input tokens with zero brake; config-free (touches no client config, only the one named session), so it applies for real in-tick like LF-6 - never pkill node, never a gateway restart

tier_notes.1: AUTO-FIX: deterministic, proven, reversible; apply immediately, report after.
tier_notes.2: FIX WITH OPERATOR STAMP: the watchdog prepares the exact command + snapshot + revert line and sends it as a one-tap proposal to the OPERATOR (never the client); an `approve <finding-id>` reply executes it.
tier_notes.3: NEVER AUTO (propose and hold): anything touching a client's model choice (sovereignty is absolute), credentials, doctrine files, deletion of anything, ambiguous findings, and any fix whose verify failed once -> Rescue Rangers with the structured escalation format.
